extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency heads and staff; Office of Management and Budget (OMB)/OIRA; Executive Office regulatory advisors; agencies developing or reviewing regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, principles, and requirements that Federal agencies (and OMB/OIRA) must follow for planning, drafting, reviewing, coordinating, and publishing regulations, including criteria for significance, cost‑benefit assessment, public participation, intergovernmental consultation, and disclosure. Covers annual planning, regulatory agendas/plans, centralized OIRA review, and review of existing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should promulgate only such regulations as are required by law, are necessary to interpret the law, or are made necessary by compelling public need (e.g., material failures of private markets to protect health, safety, environment, or well‑being). Agencies should assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives, including the alternative of not regulating; costs and benefits include quantifiable measures and qualitative measures that are difficult to quantify. In choosing among alternatives, agencies should select approaches that maximize net benefits (including economic, environmental, public health and safety, distributive impacts, and equity), unless a statute requires another approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires consideration of non‑regulatory alternatives, full cost‑benefit perspective (quantitative and qualitative), and selection of the option that maximizes net benefits subject to statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the problem and assess its significance (Principle 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify the problem it intends to address (including, where applicable, failures of private markets or public institutions) and assess the significance of that problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem definition and significance assessment are foundational steps for any regulatory action and should be explicit in agency materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine whether existing law/regulations contributed to the problem (Principle 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall examine whether existing regulations (or other law) have created or contributed to the problem a new regulation is intended to correct and whether those regulations (or other law) should be modified to achieve the intended goal more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider reforming or amending existing requirements as part of regulatory design; avoid reflexively adding new rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess alternatives to direct regulation (Principle 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including economic incentives (e.g., user fees, marketable permits) or providing information upon which choices can be made by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonregulatory and market‑based approaches must be considered and analyzed alongside prescriptive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider degree and nature of risks when setting priorities (Principle 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In setting regulatory priorities, each agency shall consider, to the extent reasonable, the degree and nature of the risks posed by various substances or activities within its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative risk considerations should inform which regulatory actions are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design regulations cost‑effectively (Principle 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a regulation is the best available method, agencies shall design regulations in the most cost‑effective manner to achieve objectives. Consider incentives for innovation, consistency, predictability, enforcement and compliance costs (to government, regulated entities, and public), flexibility, distributive impacts, and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should balance effectiveness with minimizing costs and promoting innovation and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt regulations only after reasoned determination benefits justify costs (Principle 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall assess both the costs and the benefits of the intended regulation and propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that the benefits justify its costs, recognizing some costs and benefits are difficult to quantify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision memos should record the reasoned determination and the cost‑benefit judgment, including non‑quantified effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base decisions on best reasonably obtainable information (Principle 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall base its decisions on the best reasonably obtainable scientific, technical, economic, and other information concerning the need for, and consequences of, the intended regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document evidence sources and the degree of uncertainty in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify performance objectives where feasible (Principle 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess alternative forms of regulation and shall, to the extent feasible, specify performance objectives rather than specifying the behavior or manner of compliance that regulated entities must adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor outcome‑based/performance standards that allow flexible compliance methods over prescriptive mandates when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult and minimize burdens on State/local/tribal governments (Principle 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever feasible, agencies shall seek views of appropriate State, local, and tribal officials before imposing regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect them; assess effects on their resources, seek to minimize unique/significant burdens, and harmonize Federal actions with related State/local/tribal functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should proactively engage sub‑federal governments and document consultations and burden assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative regulations (Principle 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall avoid regulations that are inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative with its other regulations or those of other Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency coordination and cross‑checks against existing rules are required to prevent duplication and inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor regulations to impose least burden (Principle 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall tailor its regulations to impose the least burden on society, including individuals, businesses of differing sizes, small communities, and governmental entities, consistent with obtaining regulatory objectives, taking into account, to the extent practicable, the costs of cumulative regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design and exemptions/thresholds should consider differential impact by size and cumulative regulatory burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft regulations simply and clearly to minimize uncertainty and litigation (Principle 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall draft its regulations to be simple and easy to understand, with the goal of minimizing the potential for uncertainty and litigation arising from such uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language drafting principles; reduce ambiguity and complexity in regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Significant regulatory action (3(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'significant regulatory action' is any regulatory action likely to result in a rule that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or adversely affect in a material way the economy, sector, productivity, competition, jobs, environment, public health or safety, or State/local/tribal governments; (2) create a serious inconsistency or interfere with action by another agency; (3) materially alter budgetary impacts of entitlements/grants/user fees/loans or rights and obligations of recipients; or (4) raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates, the President's priorities, or the principles of the Executive order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four tests to determine whether a regulatory action is 'significant' and therefore subject to heightened review and information requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies' Policy Meeting (annual planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early in each year's planning cycle, the Vice President shall convene a meeting of the Advisors and the heads of agencies to seek a common understanding of priorities and coordinate regulatory efforts for the upcoming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should prepare to present priorities and planned significant actions at this meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Regulatory Agenda requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall prepare an agenda of all regulations under development or review, containing at a minimum: a regulation identifier number, a brief summary of the action, the legal authority for the action, any legal deadline for the action, and the name and telephone number of a knowledgeable agency official. Agencies may incorporate information required under 5 U.S.C. 602 and 41 U.S.C. 402.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agendas must be prepared in the manner and time specified by the Administrator of OIRA and include independent regulatory agencies as defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan content requirements (Plan A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency's Regulatory Plan shall include at minimum: (A) a statement of the agency's regulatory objectives and priorities and relation to the President's priorities; (B) a summary of each planned significant regulatory action including alternatives and preliminary cost/benefit estimates; (C) a summary of the legal basis for each action, including whether required by statute or court order; (D) a statement of the need for each action and how it will reduce risks and relate to other risks in the agency's jurisdiction; (E) the agency's schedule for action, including statutory/judicial deadlines; (F) the name, address, and phone number of a public contact for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must be approved personally by the agency head and forwarded to OIRA by June 1 each year; Plans are published annually in the October Unified Regulatory Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan process and circulation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall forward its Plan to OIRA by June 1st. Within 10 calendar days after OIRA receives an agency's Plan, OIRA shall circulate it to other affected agencies, the Advisors, and the Vice President. Agency heads and OIRA may notify and request coordination or raise conflicts in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission and interagency circulation enable early conflict identification and possible Vice Presidential consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Working Group duties and convening
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator of OIRA shall convene a Regulatory Working Group within 30 days, consisting of representatives from agencies with significant domestic regulatory responsibility, the Advisors, and the Vice President. The Working Group shall assist in identifying/analyzing important regulatory issues (e.g., innovative techniques, comparative risk assessment, streamlined approaches for small businesses), meet at least quarterly, and may commission analytical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working Group serves as a forum for cross‑agency problem solving and methodological development.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA conferences with State/local/tribal and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA Administrator shall meet quarterly with State, local, and tribal representatives to identify regulations that may uniquely or significantly affect them, and shall convene conferences with businesses, NGOs, and the public to discuss regulatory issues of common concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured stakeholder engagement is required to identify burdens and inform regulatory planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program to review existing significant regulations (Sec. 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days, each agency shall submit to OIRA a program under which it will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any should be modified or eliminated to make the program more effective, less burdensome, or aligned with Presidential priorities and principles. Any significant regulations selected for review shall be included in the agency's annual Plan. Agencies shall also identify legislative mandates that require continued regulation that may be unnecessary or outdated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must inventory and periodically reassess older rules and propose rescissions or modifications where appropriate; solicit state/local/tribal assistance in identifying burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful public participation and comment periods (Agency responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide the public with meaningful participation in the regulatory process. Before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, agencies should, where appropriate, seek involvement of those intended to benefit and those expected to be burdened (including State/local/tribal officials). Agencies should afford the public a meaningful opportunity to comment on any proposed regulation, which in most cases should include a comment period of not less than 60 days. Agencies are directed to explore consensual mechanisms, including negotiated rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice and adequate comment time (normally ≥60 days) and early stakeholder involvement are required; alternative consensus processes encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Regulatory Policy Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days, each agency head shall designate a Regulatory Policy Officer who reports to the agency head and is involved at each stage of the regulatory process to foster development of effective, innovative, and least burdensome regulations and to further the Executive order's principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The officer acts as the internal coordinator for compliance with EO policies and OIRA interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of planned regulatory actions list to OIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide OIRA, in the manner specified, with a list of planned regulatory actions, indicating those the agency believes are significant. Absent material change, those not designated as significant will not be subject to OIRA review unless the Administrator notifies the agency within 10 working days that OIRA has determined the action is significant. OIRA may waive review of agency‑designated significant actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify significant actions early and expect a 10‑working‑day window for OIRA to designate significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to provide OIRA for significant regulatory actions (a)(3)(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each matter identified as or determined to be a significant regulatory action, the issuing agency shall provide to OIRA: (i) the text of the draft regulatory action, with a reasonably detailed description of the need for the action and an explanation of how it will meet that need; and (ii) an assessment of the potential costs and benefits of the regulatory action, including how it is consistent with statutory mandate and, to the extent permitted by law, promotes the President's priorities and avoids undue interference with State/local/tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive draft text plus needs statement and cost‑benefit assessment must be supplied to OIRA for significant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional analytical requirements for high‑impact actions (a)(3)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters determined to be significant under the economy/$100M prong (section 3(f)(1)), agencies shall provide additional information (unless prohibited by law): (i) assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated benefits with quantification to the extent feasible; (ii) assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated costs with quantification to the extent feasible; (iii) assessment and analysis of costs and benefits of potentially effective and reasonably feasible alternatives (including improving current regulation and viable nonregulatory actions) and an explanation why the planned action is preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High‑impact rules require documented benefit and cost quantification and a formal alternatives analysis explaining preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency exceptions and statutory deadline handling (a)(3)(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergency situations or when an agency is obligated by law to act more quickly than normal review allows, the agency shall notify OIRA as soon as possible and, to the extent practicable, comply with submission requirements. For rules governed by statutory or court deadlines, agencies shall, to the extent practicable, schedule rulemaking proceedings to permit sufficient time for OIRA review per section 6(b)(2)–(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must balance legal deadlines with OIRA review timelines and document any deviations or expedited notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑publication transparency obligations (a)(3)(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the regulatory action has been published or otherwise issued, the agency shall: (i) make available to the public the information provided to OIRA under (a)(3)(B) and (C); (ii) identify in a complete, clear, and simple manner substantive changes between the draft submitted to OIRA and the action announced; (iii) identify those changes that were made at the suggestion or recommendation of OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publicly disclose the analyses given to OIRA and explain changes and OIRA's role in shaping the final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for agency public materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by the agency shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication to the public must avoid jargon and be accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA may review only designated significant actions (b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA may review only actions identified by the agency or by OIRA as significant regulatory actions under subsection (a)(3)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA's review jurisdiction is limited to actions designated significant; agencies control initial designation subject to OIRA override within specified timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review timelines and waivers (b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall waive review or notify the agency in writing within: (A) 10 working days for notices of inquiry, ANPRMs, or other preliminary actions prior to an NPRM; (B) 90 calendar days for all other regulatory actions after submission of required information (or 45 days if OIRA previously reviewed the information and no material change occurred); (C) review may be extended once by up to 30 calendar days with Director approval and upon agency head request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should plan schedules around these default review clocks and request extensions only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA must provide written explanation when returning matters (b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each regulatory action the Administrator of OIRA returns to an agency for further consideration of some or all provisions, OIRA shall provide the issuing agency a written explanation setting forth the pertinent provision of the Executive order on which OIRA is relying. If the agency head disagrees, the agency head shall inform the Administrator in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written records of OIRA returns and agency disagreements are required to document basis and preserve administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA disclosure rules for external communications (b)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator of OIRA (or a particular designee) shall receive oral communications initiated by persons not employed by the executive branch regarding the substance of a regulatory action under OIRA review. All substantive communications between OIRA personnel and non‑federal persons shall: (i) invite a representative from the issuing agency to any meeting; (ii) have OIRA forward to the issuing agency within 10 working days all written communications received from non‑federal persons and the dates and names of individuals involved in substantive oral communications; (iii) be publicly disclosed as set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes strict rules to ensure transparency and agency inclusion in off‑record contacts with outside parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA public log and document disclosure (b)(4)(C)–(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall maintain a publicly available log containing at minimum: status of regulatory actions (including Vice Presidential/Presidential consideration notation); notation of written communications forwarded to issuing agency; dates and names of individuals involved in substantive oral communications and subject matter discussed. After publication or announcement of an action (or decision not to publish), OIRA shall make available to the public all documents exchanged between OIRA and the agency during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a public record of OIRA interactions and interagency exchanges to promote openness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for OIRA public materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by OIRA shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA communications must be accessible to non‑technical audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of conflicts via Vice President/President (Sec. 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreements between agency heads or between OMB and any agency unresolved by the Administrator of OIRA shall be resolved by the President, or by the Vice President at the President's request. Vice Presidential/Presidential consideration may be initiated only by the Director or by the head of the issuing agency or by the head of an agency with significant interest. Development of recommendations shall be concluded within 60 days after review has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides escalation path and a 60‑day decision target; restricts who may request Presidential consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of communications during VP/Presidential review
rubrics_metrics.description: During Vice Presidential and Presidential review, communications with any person not employed by the Federal Government relating to the substance of the regulatory action and directed to the Advisors or their staffs or to Vice President staff shall be in writing and forwarded by the recipient to the affected agency for inclusion in the public docket(s). If the communication is not in writing, staff shall inform the outside party that the matter is under review and that comments should be submitted in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures outside contacts during high‑level review are placed into the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on publication pending OIRA review completion (Sec. 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall not publish in the Federal Register or otherwise issue to the public any regulatory action subject to review under section 6 until (1) OIRA notifies the agency that it has waived review or completed review without requests for further consideration, or (2) the applicable time period in section 6(b)(2) expires without OIRA notifying the agency that it is returning the action for further consideration, whichever occurs first. If terms are not satisfied and agency wants to publish, the agency head may request Presidential consideration via the Vice President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is generally stayed until OIRA review completes or time lapses; agencies must follow procedures to request exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority and judicial review clarifications (Secs. 9–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the order shall be construed as displacing agencies' authority or responsibilities as authorized by law. Nothing shall affect otherwise available judicial review of agency action; the Executive order is intended only to improve internal management and does not create any enforceable rights or benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO establishes internal management requirements but does not create private rights or alter statutory authority or judicial review rights.
